identity.name: Royal Oak
identity.one_liner: The 1972 original: Genta's octagonal steel watch at a gold price, the design that saved Audemars Piguet.

narrative.story: In 1971 AP asked Gerald Genta for a steel sports watch overnight; the story goes that he delivered the Royal Oak by morning — an octagonal bezel held by eight visible hexagonal screws, inspired by a diver's helmet, on an integrated bracelet. Launched at Basel 1972 at CHF 3,300, roughly ten times a contemporary steel watch, it was ridiculed, then it rescued a company being strangled by the quartz crisis. Production of the 5402 ran to about 1990 across A, B, C and D series, only a few thousand pieces in total, all on the ultra-thin caliber 2121.
narrative.collector_notes: A-series examples (AP monogram at 6, earliest casebacks) are the blue chips; series identification via case numbers is the first authentication step. Dial replacements during AP service were common for decades — original 'petite tapisserie' with correct printing drives the price gap.
